summary: Sudan requires an embassy visa obtained in advance for nearly every nationality, but the civil war that began in April 2023 has effectively closed the country to tourism. Many Sudanese missions abroad have suspended or scaled back visa services, and Western governments advise against all travel.

AF.notes: A visa must be obtained in advance from a Sudanese embassy. The embassy in Washington issues entry visas only for business or official travel, backed by a letter from a sponsoring organisation, and many Sudanese missions abroad have scaled back visa services since the civil war began. The embassy in Berlin issues tourist visas once a registered tour agency or sponsor in Sudan has obtained an entry-permit number from the Ministry of the Interior.

Australia's Smartraveller says you need a permit for photography of any kind, and that even with one you may not photograph military areas, infrastructure or slums.

payments.text: Canada's travel advice says foreign debit and credit cards are not accepted, ATMs serve only local accounts, and international flights and hotel bills must be paid in cash, so bring enough US dollars for your stay. The UK government adds that only US dollar notes dated 2006 or later may be exchanged.

safety.text: Sudan has been in armed conflict since April 2023. The UK advises against all travel to Sudan (all but essential travel for the Hala'ib Triangle and the Bir Tawil Trapezoid) and Canada says to avoid all travel. The British Embassy in Khartoum is closed, and the UK says it cannot provide in-person consular support inside Sudan.

tips.text: Sudan is in armed conflict and governments advise against all travel. Canada's travel advice says drone attacks occur frequently nationwide and that the airports at Port Sudan and Khartoum may close without notice.
Many Sudanese embassies and consulates have suspended or scaled back visa services since the war began. Check whether the mission serving your country is actually operating before planning anything.

Canada's travel advice says foreigners must register with the Ministry of the Interior's Aliens' Registration Office within 3 days of arrival (some larger hotels do it for a fee), and the UK government says you need a travel permit, applied for in the country, to leave the Red Sea State.
Canada's travel advice says the authorities will automatically deny you entry if your passport contains an Israeli stamp.

faq.question: Do I need a visa for Sudan?
faq.answer: Yes — nearly every nationality needs a visa obtained in advance from a Sudanese embassy. The embassy in Washington issues entry visas only for business or official travel, backed by a letter from a sponsoring organisation, and many Sudanese missions abroad are not processing applications because of the civil war.

faq.question: Is Sudan open to tourists?
faq.answer: Effectively no. Canada's travel advice says heavy fighting has continued across the country since April 2023 and drone attacks occur frequently, and Western governments advise against all travel.

faq.question: Does Sudan have an eVisa or visa on arrival?
faq.answer: No reliable one. Visas are issued in advance by Sudanese embassies; any on-arrival arrangements that existed before the war cannot be counted on. Confirm directly with a functioning Sudanese mission.

faq.question: Can Israeli citizens visit Sudan?
faq.answer: No — Israeli passport holders are not admitted to Sudan. The UK and Canada add that you will be refused entry if your passport contains an Israeli visa or entry or exit stamp.

faq.question: Which Sudanese embassy should I apply through?
faq.answer: Normally the mission accredited to your country of residence, but since the war many have suspended services, so you may need to contact several to find one that is operating. Requirements and fees vary considerably between missions.
